Raised.description: The total amount raised for this campaign. When RaisedCalculationMode is SoftCreditPledgeAdjusted, a donation whose soft credit paid down a pledge contributes only the remainder here, so this total is lower than the Legacy figure for the same campaign. The pledge normally contributes the rest; see RaisedCalculationMode for the written-off and overpaid cases where it does not. Always read that field alongside this one before comparing campaigns across databases or against a previously reported number.

RaisedCalculationMode.description:
Which formula produced the Raised value in this response. This is not a fixed property of the API: the corrected calculation is being rolled out one database at a time, so the same endpoint can return one mode for one organization and the other mode for another at the same moment.
SoftCreditPledgeAdjusted means the donation side subtracts any soft credits on the entry that pay down a pledge, floored at zero, so Raised can legitimately be less than Revenue. In the ordinary case the pledge reports that money instead and it stops being counted twice. Do not treat that as a guaranteed conservation, though: the two sides are computed independently rather than handed from one to the other, and a pledge that has been written off or overpaid absorbs less than the donation gave up, leaving the difference reported by neither side.
Legacy means the older behaviour: Raised equals Revenue for non-pledge entries, and a soft credit that pays a pledge is counted both on the pledge and again on the donation it came from, so any total that combines the two counts that money twice.
Do not compare or add Raised figures that carry different modes, and say which basis you used when reporting a total. If this field is absent the number came from a cached summary written before the mode was recorded, and which formula produced it is unknown.

IsPledgePaymentViaSoftCredit.description: True when a soft credit on this designation was applied to a pledge and has therefore reduced Raised below Revenue. Equivalent to checking Raised != Revenue, precomputed. Always false when RaisedCalculationMode is Legacy, because that mode never reduces Raised. Use it to explain a Raised that looks too low, or to find the donations whose credit has moved to a pledge.

QuickBooksOnlineStatus.description: If the QuickBooks Online integration is enabled, this is the QBO status of the designation

Raised.description: The amount this designation counts toward fundraising credit. It is normally equal to Revenue, but it is LOWER than Revenue when a soft credit on this designation was applied to a pledge: the amount is subtracted here so that it is not counted both on this donation and on the pledge it paid. A Raised below Revenue is expected in that case rather than a refund or a data-entry error. Never negative (floored at 0). Null for entry types that do not count toward raised, such as a pledge payment. Read RaisedCalculationMode before comparing or summing this figure across databases -- the two modes are computed on different bases, and it also records the cases where the pledge does not take up what was subtracted here.

RaisedCalculationMode.description:
Which formula produced the Raised value in this response. This is not a fixed property of the API: the corrected calculation is being rolled out one database at a time, so the same endpoint can return one mode for one organization and the other mode for another at the same moment.
SoftCreditPledgeAdjusted means the donation side subtracts any soft credits on the entry that pay down a pledge, floored at zero, so Raised can legitimately be less than Revenue. In the ordinary case the pledge reports that money instead and it stops being counted twice. Do not treat that as a guaranteed conservation, though: the two sides are computed independently rather than handed from one to the other, and a pledge that has been written off or overpaid absorbs less than the donation gave up, leaving the difference reported by neither side.
Legacy means the older behaviour: Raised equals Revenue for non-pledge entries, and a soft credit that pays a pledge is counted both on the pledge and again on the donation it came from, so any total that combines the two counts that money twice.
Do not compare or add Raised figures that carry different modes, and say which basis you used when reporting a total. If this field is absent the number came from a cached summary written before the mode was recorded, and which formula produced it is unknown.

Revenue.description: The money actually received for this designation. 0 if the transaction was refunded. Null for entry types that are not received money, such as a pledge, which is a promise to give. Soft credits never change this value, so comparing it with Raised tells you whether any of this designation's money was credited to a pledge.

IsPledgePaymentViaSoftCredit.description: True when a soft credit on this designation was applied to a pledge and has therefore reduced Raised below Revenue. Equivalent to checking Raised != Revenue, precomputed. Always false when RaisedCalculationMode is Legacy, because that mode never reduces Raised. Use it to explain a Raised that looks too low, or to find the donations whose credit has moved to a pledge.

QuickBooksOnlineStatus.description: If the QuickBooks Online integration is enabled, this is the QBO status of the designation

Raised.description: The amount this designation counts toward fundraising credit. It is normally equal to Revenue, but it is LOWER than Revenue when a soft credit on this designation was applied to a pledge: the amount is subtracted here so that it is not counted both on this donation and on the pledge it paid. A Raised below Revenue is expected in that case rather than a refund or a data-entry error. Never negative (floored at 0). Null for entry types that do not count toward raised, such as a pledge payment. Read RaisedCalculationMode before comparing or summing this figure across databases -- the two modes are computed on different bases, and it also records the cases where the pledge does not take up what was subtracted here.

RaisedCalculationMode.description:
Which formula produced the Raised value in this response. This is not a fixed property of the API: the corrected calculation is being rolled out one database at a time, so the same endpoint can return one mode for one organization and the other mode for another at the same moment.
SoftCreditPledgeAdjusted means the donation side subtracts any soft credits on the entry that pay down a pledge, floored at zero, so Raised can legitimately be less than Revenue. In the ordinary case the pledge reports that money instead and it stops being counted twice. Do not treat that as a guaranteed conservation, though: the two sides are computed independently rather than handed from one to the other, and a pledge that has been written off or overpaid absorbs less than the donation gave up, leaving the difference reported by neither side.
Legacy means the older behaviour: Raised equals Revenue for non-pledge entries, and a soft credit that pays a pledge is counted both on the pledge and again on the donation it came from, so any total that combines the two counts that money twice.
Do not compare or add Raised figures that carry different modes, and say which basis you used when reporting a total. If this field is absent the number came from a cached summary written before the mode was recorded, and which formula produced it is unknown.

Revenue.description: The money actually received for this designation. 0 if the transaction was refunded. Null for entry types that are not received money, such as a pledge, which is a promise to give. Soft credits never change this value, so comparing it with Raised tells you whether any of this designation's money was credited to a pledge.
